claims.text: HPHT treatment can improve the balance of strength and ductility of Co-free FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.
The proposed starting material is an as-cast or homogenized Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The proposed intervention is HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
The HPHT treatment will produce a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The HPHT-produced microstructure will contain coherent interfaces.
The hierarchically patterned microstructure will allow dislocations to transfer between phases.
Dislocation transfer between phases will relieve stress concentrations.
Dislocation transfer and stress relief will prevent interfacial cracking.
The HPHT-induced microstructure will progressively activate multiple deformation mechanisms at multiple length scales.
HPHT treatment will double tensile strength relative to the untreated precursor alloy.
HPHT treatment will double tensile ductility relative to the untreated precursor alloy.
The predicted improvement is valid from room temperature to 1000 K.
The predicted improvement is valid over strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^8 s^-1.
Mechanical behavior may depend on processing conditions, alloy composition, and testing parameters.
The proposed falsification test is a room-temperature uniaxial tensile test at 3 × 10^-4 s^-1 comparing treated and precursor alloys.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a doubling of both properties, whereas the falsification rule only requires an undefined 'significant improvement,' so the test criterion does not match the quantitative prediction.
